service: Atlassian (Confluence and Jira, Rovo MCP server)

facts.claim: The current hosted MCP endpoint is the v2 URL on mcp.atlassian.com
facts.evidence: Getting-started lists https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp as the default endpoint; the vendor's protected-resource document reports resource https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp.

facts.claim: These scope names are real Rovo MCP scopes: read/search per product under the agent-interface naming, plus read:me
facts.evidence: Supported tools lists read:jira:agent-interface, search:jira:agent-interface, read/search:confluence:agent-interface; the protected-resource document's scopes_supported also lists them and read:me.

facts.claim: Sign-in involves mcp.atlassian.com and the authorization server on auth.atlassian.com
facts.evidence: authorization_servers is https://auth.atlassian.com/<tenant path>; the docs pages fetched name only mcp.atlassian.com.

facts.claim: The authorization server publishes a dynamic client registration endpoint, so the client registers itself (mcp-oauth, not preregistered); S256 PKCE is supported
facts.evidence: registration_endpoint is https://auth.atlassian.com/<tenant path>/dcr/register; code_challenge_methods_supported is S256. No docs page mentions dynamic registration.

facts.claim: v2 reached general availability on 8 September 2026; v1 usage is moved onto v2 tools from 1 March 2027
facts.evidence: "On Mar 1, 2027 any existing utilization of v1 will automatically start to expose and utilize v2 tools."

facts.claim: No current Atlassian page mentions an SSE endpoint (/v1/sse); the docs use transport http only
facts.evidence: Page configures "type":"http" and does not mention SSE (absence of mention, not an explicit retirement notice).

facts.claim: OAuth 2.1 is the primary sign-in; API token auth (personal token or service account key) exists only if an organization admin enables it
facts.evidence: "Requires admin enablement" for API token; the support.atlassian.com getting-started page also lists OAuth 2.1 with optional admin-controlled API token.

facts.claim: delete_jira and manage_jira groups are disabled by default and admin-gated; search_code and Teams are OAuth only; JSM tools are API token only
facts.evidence: Supported tools marks delete_jira and manage_jira "disabled by default, admin-gated"; the authentication page repeats this.

facts.claim: Write tools: createJiraIssue, editJiraIssue, transitionJiraIssue, addOrEditJiraIssueComment, delete* group, createConfluenceContent, updateConfluenceContent, executeWrite, executeDestructive and others; the template asks first for all but transitionJiraIssue and addOrEditJiraIssueComment, which the owner keeps as ordinary writes
facts.evidence: Tool catalog names these in write_jira, delete_jira, manage_jira, write_confluence and the core execute tools.

facts.claim: atlassianUserInfo is a core tool available to both auth methods and is the candidate smoke read
facts.evidence: Listed under Common/core as primary; page does not document its inputs.

facts.claim: No plan or admin-approval requirement is stated for OAuth; Rovo credits apply to some tools; whiteboard and attachment tools need api.media.atlassian.com and *.frontend.public.atl-paas.net reachable
facts.evidence: Page lists no prerequisites but says some tools consume Rovo credits and names those two allowlist domains.

choices.decision: Archetype mcp-oauth (hosted URL, browser sign-in, automatic registration), with the v2 URL
choices.because: Docs give a hosted OAuth 2.1 endpoint and the authorization server advertises dynamic registration; the API-token route is admin-gated and left out

choices.decision: Request only read and search scopes plus read:me
choices.because: Narrowest useful set; write scopes can be added with re-consent

choices.decision: Consent list built from the write, delete and manage tool names
choices.because: Those tools create, edit, move, share or delete content

open: No documentation page says that /v1/sse (SSE) is deprecated or retired; it is simply absent from current pages. Not confirmed either way.
The support.atlassian.com page names the v1 URL only inside a Cursor install link, and another Atlassian guide still shows v1 examples; developer.atlassian.com (v2) was treated as current.
Dynamic client registration is shown only by the discovery document, not by any docs page; whether it is open to any client was not tested (no request to the endpoint).
The authorization server URL contains a vendor tenant path that may change; only auth.atlassian.com is pinned.
Plan tier, whether a site admin must approve the OAuth app first, and the exact redirect URI rules for a loopback client are not stated on the pages read.
Whether atlassianUserInfo needs no input and works with read:me alone is unconfirmed; it may need read:account.
The page mentions Compass only as an entity type in Teamwork Graph; no Compass tool group exists in the catalog.
The consent globs assume LOTR matches tool names as written; the Remix and infographic Confluence tools also match createConfluence*/editConfluence*.
